title: The Shoah: mechanisms of genocide
subject: histoire
description: Between **1941** and **1945**, the Nazi regime organized the assassination of six million Jews. The Shoah is not an explosion of spontaneous hatred, but a state process.

hero.hook: Understand how a modern state transformed persecution into extermination.

blocks.text: Between **1941** and **1945**, the Nazi regime orchestrated the assassination of **6 million Jews**, or two-thirds of the Jews in Europe. In Hebrew, **Holocaust** means “catastrophe.”
This genocide is not disorderly violence. It is a state process, organized step by step: from legal exclusion to industrial killing.

From **January 1933**, when **Adolf Hitler** came to power, the Nazi state put anti-Semitism into law. The Nuremberg Laws (**1935**) deprived Jews of citizenship and prohibited mixed unions. In November **1938**, “Kristallnacht”, an organized  (violent attack against a Jewish community), saw synagogues burned and **30,000** men interned. **[[pogrom]]**

After the invasion of Poland (**1939**), the Nazis imposed the **[[ghettoization]]**: Jews were locked up in closed neighborhoods, particularly in Warsaw and Łódź. Famine, epidemics, isolation: an already massive destruction, still indirect.

blocks.caption: Auschwitz-Birkenau, which has become the symbol of the extermination system.

sections.title: The invasion of the USSR and the shootings

blocks.text: On **June 22, 1941**, Nazi Germany launches Operation Barbarossa against the USSR. In the wake of the Wehrmacht (the German army), the **[[The Einsatzgruppen]]**, mobile units of the SS, assassinated communists and Jewish populations.

In approximately **18 months**, these commandos killed nearly **1.5 million** people. At Babi Yar, near kyiv, in September **1941**, **33 771** Jews are shot in two days. The method is considered too slow, too visible, too taxing for the performers. The regime is seeking a more anonymous system.

sections.title: Wannsee: organizing murder on a European scale

blocks.text: **January 20, 1942**,  brings together **15** senior Nazi officials near Berlin. It is no longer a question of deciding the principle of extermination, already established, but of organizing the deportation of all the Jews of Europe: trains, administrations, logistics. [[The Wannsee Conference (January 1942)]]

blocks.caption: Wannsee Villa, where the “Final Solution” was coordinated.

blocks.text: Belzec, Sobibor, Treblinka, Auschwitz-Birkenau become killing centers. On the ramp, a “selection” separates a minority destined for forced labor from the majority taken immediately to the gas chambers. The philosopher **Hannah Arendt** will later speak about : extermination managed as an administrative problem. **[[The "banality of evil" (Hannah Arendt)]]**
The Wannsee conference, which coordinates the continental scale of crime, lasts approximately **90 minutes**.

Of **9 million** pre-war European Jews, two thirds disappear. Poland loses approximately **90%** of its Jewish population. The regime also persecutes the **[[Gypsies]]** (Roma and Sinti), people with disabilities, homosexuals, political opponents. The Shoah remains unique in its desire for the total and systematic destruction of a people.

The Nuremberg trial then attempted to legally name this crime. Places like , a memory institute in Jerusalem, maintain memory so that this state mechanism is neither forgotten nor trivialized. **[[Yad Vashem]]**

blocks.text: The Shoah was the assassination of **6 million** Jews by a state system: legal exclusion, ghettos, shootings, then killing centers. An organized genocide, not a spontaneous explosion.
